checkpoints.description: [1/1] Audit implementation, fix scan-error handling and typing gaps, verify, then publish/push

impact_assessment.why: The audit found a false-success exit code on incomplete scans, an unhandled root failure, and 32 lint findings; the user also asked to push.
impact_assessment.benefits: A scan that could not read everything now fails loudly, a vanished root gets a clean error, and the code is clean under Ruff.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: exit 1 now also means an incomplete scan; dependency: standard library only; concurrency: read-only scan with no shared state; state: publishing creates a GitHub repository and pushes commits
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add regression tests for both failure paths, record ADR-003, run all gates, and publish private unless the user chooses public.

[1/1] Add human-readable size bounds and exclude-file support; update tests, docs, version and gates

impact_assessment.why: Real scans need natural size limits and reusable exclusion lists instead of long command lines or manual byte arithmetic.
impact_assessment.benefits: Users can pass --min-size 1MiB and --max-size 500M, and keep shared ignore patterns in a file with comments and blank lines.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new --max-size and --exclude-from flags plus a version bump; dependency: standard library re and pathlib only; concurrency: read-only scan with no shared state; state: no file writes outside the project
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep parsing strict, validate max >= min, test suffixes, comments and unreadable files, document 1024-based units, and run every project gate before committing.

[1/1] Add --redundant-list FILE for safe cleanup planning; update tests, docs, version and gates

impact_assessment.why: Finding duplicates is useful, but users still need a reviewable list of which copies are redundant without risking automatic deletion.
impact_assessment.benefits: Users can write one path per redundant copy to a file, keep the first path in each group, and review the list before deleting anything.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new output flag and CSV/JSON stay unchanged; dependency: standard library only; concurrency: read-only scan plus one report-file write; state: the output file must never overwrite a scanned file
impact_assessment.mitigation: Refuse output paths that resolve to scanned files, create an empty list when there are no duplicates, report write failures cleanly, test each path, and run every gate before pushing.

[1/1] Add --keep strategies for redundant lists; update tests, docs, version and gates

impact_assessment.why: Keeping the first path is deterministic but arbitrary; users need to preserve a canonical, shortest, oldest or newest copy when reviewing duplicates.
impact_assessment.benefits: The redundant list can keep the shortest path, the original oldest copy, or the newest copy, while still never deleting anything.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new --keep flag tied to --redundant-list; dependency: standard library pathlib stat only; concurrency: read-only scan plus one list write; state: oldest/newest read file timestamps and must fail cleanly if they vanish
impact_assessment.mitigation: Validate --keep requires --redundant-list, break ties by shortest then lexicographic path, test each strategy with controlled mtimes, catch stat failures, and run every gate before pushing.
